**Session ID:** `01KJQT6EXAE3K8FTB2GW2ECCYF`
**Iteration:** 1 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)

> **Truncated** (103618 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Implement Agent Dispatch Engine
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJP277R7TP3HWHAMNEV2ZSB3
Slugs:     implement-agent-dispatch-engine
Type:      task
Status:    needs_work
Priority:  3
Automation: eligible
Spec ref:  @agent-dispatch-engine
Plan ref:  @plan-reactive-agent-runtime
Depends:
  @implement-agent-invocation-lifecycle → Implement Agent Invocation Lifecycle [completed]
Created:   2026-03-02T01:22:21.575Z
Started:   2026-03-02T16:55:01.563Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Dispatch Engine
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
  state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
  emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
  dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
  deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
  mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits


─── Notes ───
[2026-03-02T01:22:21.575Z] @claude:
Implementation notes:

New module at src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. In-memory queue with
configurable concurrency. Event deduplication via a Map of recent
(task_id, from_state, to_state) tuples with TTL (e.g. 2 seconds).
Bootstrap on start: load all tasks, evaluate dispatch rules, queue
matches. Shadow branch serialization: wrap kspec CLI mutations in
a queue/lock when concurrent agents are running. Task state diffing
stores previous parsed states in memory, compares on file change.

[2026-03-02T04:39:11.298Z] @claude:
Automation: eligible. Complex but well-specified with 12 ACs. Implementation notes cover queue design, dedup strategy, bootstrap behavior.
[2026-03-02T17:12:54.687Z] @claude:
Implemented DispatchEngine in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. Key design decisions:

- In-memory queue with FIFO dispatch per agent, respecting max_concurrent limit
- Event deduplication via (task_id, from_state, to_state) tuple with configurable TTL (default 2s)
- Bootstrap on start: loads all tasks, evaluates dispatch rules, queues matches
- File watcher integration via FileChangeCallback in ProjectContextManager (avoids tight coupling)
- Shadow branch serialization via simple in-house Mutex (no external dep)
- specDir is configurable to support both shadow (.kspec/) and traditional mode
- Daemon routes at /api/agent/dispatch/start|stop|status and /api/agent/event (AC-4)
- 18 behavioral tests covering all 12 ACs
[2026-03-02T17:37:46.898Z] Jacob Chapel:
[FIX_CYCLE: 1] Review findings: PR #634 review findings: MUST-FIX AC gaps in dispatch engine (retry queue can stall without wake-up, unresolved adapter path does not add required task note, stop() does not send graceful cancel signals, filter matching is bypassed when task data is missing). Additional SHOULD-FIX items on prompt double-expansion and input validation posted inline. Not merged.

─── Inherited from @trait-error-guidance ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: command encounters error
    When: error message is shown
    Then: includes description of what went wrong
  [ac-2] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: command encounters error
    When: error message is shown
    Then: includes suggested action to resolve
  [ac-3] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: reference not found
    When: error is shown
    Then: suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
  [ac-4] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: invalid state transition
    When: error is shown
    Then: indicates current state and valid next states
  [ac-5] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: validation error
    When: error is shown
    Then: indicates which field/value failed validation
  [ac-6] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: error in JSON mode
    When: --json is active
    Then: guidance included in structured error object

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Dispatch Engine
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
  state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
  emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
  dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
  deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
  mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits

Started:   2026-03-02T16:55:01.563Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Dispatch Engine
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
  state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
  emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
  dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
  deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
  mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits


─── Notes ───
[2026-03-02T01:22:21.575Z] @claude:
Implementation notes:

New module at src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. In-memory queue with
configurable concurrency. Event deduplication via a Map of recent
(task_id, from_state, to_state) tuples with TTL (e.g. 2 seconds).
Bootstrap on start: load all tasks, evaluate dispatch rules, queue
matches. Shadow branch serialization: wrap kspec CLI mutations in
a queue/lock when concurrent agents are running. Task state diffing
stores previous parsed states in memory, compares on file change.

[2026-03-02T04:39:11.298Z] @claude:
Automation: eligible. Complex but well-specified with 12 ACs. Implementation notes cover queue design, dedup strategy, bootstrap behavior.
[2026-03-02T17:12:54.687Z] @claude:
Implemented DispatchEngine in src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. Key design decisions:

- In-memory queue with FIFO dispatch per agent, respecting max_concurrent limit
- Event deduplication via (task_id, from_state, to_state) tuple with configurable TTL (default 2s)
- Bootstrap on start: loads all tasks, evaluates dispatch rules, queues matches
- File watcher integration via FileChangeCallback in ProjectContextManager (avoids tight coupling)
- Shadow branch serialization via simple in-house Mutex (no external dep)
- specDir is configurable to support both shadow (.kspec/) and traditional mode
- Daemon routes at /api/agent/dispatch/start|stop|status and /api/agent/event (AC-4)
- 18 behavioral tests covering all 12 ACs
[2026-03-02T17:37:46.898Z] Jacob Chapel:
[FIX_CYCLE: 1] Review findings: PR #634 review findings: MUST-FIX AC gaps in dispatch engine (retry queue can stall without wake-up, unresolved adapter path does not add required task note, stop() does not send graceful cancel signals, filter matching is bypassed when task data is missing). Additional SHOULD-FIX items on prompt double-expansion and input validation posted inline. Not merged.

    Given: command encounters error
    When: error message is shown
    Then: includes description of what went wrong
  [ac-2] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: command encounters error
    When: error message is shown
    Then: includes suggested action to resolve
  [ac-3] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: reference not found
    When: error is shown
    Then: suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
  [ac-4] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: invalid state transition
    When: error is shown
    Then: indicates current state and valid next states
  [ac-5] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: validation error
    When: error is shown
    Then: indicates which field/value failed validation
  [ac-6] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: error in JSON mode
    When: --json is active
    Then: guidance included in structured error object

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,

only once

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    When: Active agent invocations exist
